ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a large rectangle ABCD, with A at the lower left corner, B at the lower right corner, C at the upper right corner, and D at the upper left corner. The inside of the large rectangle is divided into three congruent small rectangles: on the left there are two horizontal small rectangles stacked one above the other, and on the right there is one vertical small rectangle, whose height is equal to the height of the entire large rectangle. Reasoning: Let the short side of each small rectangle be s, and the long side be l. The problem gives the short side s = 5 feet. According to the image, the height of the vertical small rectangle on the right is l, while the total height of the two horizontal small rectangles stacked on the left is s + s = 2s. Because they are both equal to the height of the large rectangle ABCD, l = 2s = 10. The height of the large rectangle is 10, and the width is the long side of the small rectangle on the left plus the short side of the small rectangle on the right, namely l + s = 10 + 5 = 15. Therefore the area of the large rectangle ABCD is 10 × 15 = 150 square feet.

method.method_draft: Describe the image first: rectangle ABCD is partitioned into three congruent smaller rectangles, with two congruent rectangles stacked one above the other on the left and one congruent rectangle standing vertically on the right. Let the shorter side of a small rectangle be s and the longer side be l. From the text, s=5. From the image, the full height of ABCD equals the height of the right rectangle, which is l, and also equals the combined heights of the two stacked left rectangles, which is s+s=2s. Thus l=2s=10. The outer rectangle then has height 10 and width l+s=10+5=15, so its area is 10*15=150.
